messages:
sam: heads up — getting multiple customer escalations about 503s and timeouts starting ~2034501200. They all hit the hosted inference endpoint in us-west-2.
maya: @sam can you paste a few request ids/trace ids? is this a canary rollout?
sam: yes this rolled out a traffic-split yesterday morning (10% -> 50%). repro traces: trace=trc_8f3a1, trc_8f3a2, trc_8f3a7. sample error: `upstream response 503` and `gateway timeout 504`.
alex: paging oncall — maya is oncall today. maya: I see elevated 5xx rate in the dashboards, spike start ~2034501180. Error tag looks like `model-proxy: upstream 503`.
maya: checking canary config now. jenkins-deploy shows feature flag 'serve-v2-kernel' ramp from 10 to 50 at 2034501100.
jordan: that flag toggles the new batching pipeline + kernel selection. we toggled it to reduce cost.
lee: customers reporting latency & HTTP 503, one customer provided curl sample and response body: `{\n  "error": "model unavailable",\n  "code": 503\n}`
sam: support ticket ids: SUP-912, SUP-915, SUP-918. All hit endpoints /v1/generate with prompt lengths ~1200 tokens.
maya: looking at pod logs on the canary pool: lots of `kv cache thrash` warnings and OOMs in a subset of instances.
alex: can you paste the relevant log lines?
maya: paste: ```\n2026-03-15T12:02:13Z model-proxy[canary-23]: warn: KV cache miss ratio high for session=abc123\n2026-03-15T12:02:14Z model-proxy[canary-23]: error: worker crashed, OOM\n2026-03-15T12:02:14Z kubelet: Back-off restarting failed container\n``` 
jordan: hmm v2 kernel uses a different KV cache layout, we did not fully validate large-context workloads. Could be memory pressure.
sam: quick ask from support: can we reduce traffic to canary and route back to stable? Customers are getting bill-impacting failures.
maya: issuing rollback of traffic-split to 0% for v2 via routing control plane now. running command: `./trafficctl set-split serve-v2 0 --env hosted --region us-west-2`.
deploy-bot: canary rollout change submitted by maya: set-split serve-v2 0 -> pending.
ops-bot: rollback approval required from eng-lead. @jordan please +1.
jordan: +1, go for rollback.
deploy-bot: rollback applied — serve-v2 now 0% in us-west-2. change id: ch_2034501299
maya: I'm seeing 5xx drop immediately on the stable pools, latency returning to baseline for many customers. still monitoring.
alex: good. can you collect heap dumps from one of the failing canary nodes before it's torn down? we need postmortem material.
maya: pulled heap dump and model-proxy core from canary-23. uploading to s3://redwood-debug/dumps/2034501234-canary-23.tar.gz
sam: replied to customers with rollback update and ETA for root cause analysis. customers asked for timeline; I told them we expect a detailed incident update in 6 hours.
jordan: follow-ups: (1) add load test for long-context >1k tokens against v2 kernel, (2) run canary at <5% for longer with synthetic traces, (3) add memory pressure alerts per-pool.
lee: looping in CS for any affected accounts for credits and comms; tagging accounts in SUP-912/915/918.
maya: creating incident ticket INC-2034501 and assigning to eng-runtime team for triage.
alex: thanks team — keep posting any anomalies. we should coordinate a quick blameless postmortem later today. closing the immediate severity to sev-2 since traffic rolled back and customer impact reduced.
sam: ACK — will update thread with postmortem link when available. :thumbsup:
